content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an in-app AI agent and a local MCP server (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/`), plus a stdio bridge binary (`jusprin-mcp`, `Mcp/Bridge/`) that external clients like Claude Code launch; the bridge finds the running app through a discovery file and forwards calls over loopback HTTP. Because these tests hang, two sessions so far have excluded them ("~MCP bridge*" or "~[mcp]") to get full-suite counts, which hides whatever is wrong. Project test rule (agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md): record pre-existing failures by exact name and failure mode, rerun in isolation, and treat repeatable failures as regressions until disproved. Shared-Mac build rules: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`, one build per build dir, `-- -j4`, Release config, configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` first on PATH (see the `jusprin-worktree-build` memory), absolute build-dir paths, kill your own ninja before ending a turn.

Task:
The 7 "MCP bridge ..." cases in `tests/agent/test_mcp_bridge.cpp` (target `agent_bridge_tests`) fail on this Mac, then hang forever in the test `Harness` destructor. Found 2026-10-28/29 on local `jusprin-newui` 953eddb355, with and without the Bash sandbox, with no other test process running.

Already established with temporary instrumentation (all reverted):
- The app side starts fine: `McpRuntime` writes a valid discovery file (`url` `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`), and `Mcp::read_discovery` reads it back OK.
- The bridge's liveness probe (`route()` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/Bridge/Bridge.cpp`, a `server/discover` sent through `HttpExchange`) fails with "The local MCP request timed out." The bridge then answers `workspace_unavailable` ("Open JusPrin and a project…"). `route()`'s failure callback discards that reason.
- Raising the test's probe timeout from 200 ms to 2000 ms does not help, so the request never completes; it is not slow. `McpServer` answers `server/discover` on its own io thread, so it does not wait on the test's polling.
- Plain loopback HTTP between processes works on this Mac (python http.server + curl: 3 ms). The `test_mcp_runtime.cpp` cases, which talk to the same server through the test client, pass. Active network extension: IPVanish WireGuard; the LuLu and Cisco socket filters are installed but not enabled.

Next: find where the bridge's request stops (does `async_connect` complete; does `McpServer` accept it and read the request; does it reply), for example with `nettop`/`lsof` or logging in `HttpExchange.cpp` and `McpServer.cpp`. Compare against how `tests/agent/mcp_test_client.hpp` connects, since that works. Also find why a failed case hangs in `~Harness` instead of failing. Check `git log` for when these tests last passed. Fix the cause (bridge, server or harness). Done: the 7 cases pass several times in random order, the full binary finishes, and one commit states cause, fix and test counts. Reproduce before fixing (project rule).

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_b36c90ea-ddca-4ce3-ad0d-3fe4b39cfef5

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

# M3: tool record rewritten after the model saw it (session tool-record-terminal)

Commit cc5c12f9ff on branch claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2 (based on local jusprin-newui 953eddb355, unmerged, unpushed).

Reproduced: a call whose project save after it throws was sent to the model as "succeeded"; the stored record and every later replay said "failed / local_save_failed".
Fix: ToolExecutionCoordinator holds back a call's terminal notification while its post-run save is pending (m_saving_after), then announces once. fail() throws std::logic_error on a record already announced as finished.

## MCP bridge tests hang on this machine (not caused by M3)

The 7 "MCP bridge ..." cases in agent_bridge_tests (tests/agent/test_mcp_bridge.cpp) fail (isError true, no edits) and then hang in Harness::~Harness (__ulock_wait, ~0 CPU) on 2026-10-28, with HEAD's coordinator as well as with the fix. Inside the Bash sandbox they also log "Permission denied" removing the temp mcp.json. A full run of the binary therefore never finishes; run with the filter "~MCP bridge*" to get the rest (463 cases passed here). The cache-invariant session's full run (PID 2958) was hung at the same time, probably the same cause.

## Update 2026-10-29: where the MCP bridge tests fail

The discovery file is written and read fine. The bridge's liveness probe (`server/discover` over loopback HTTP to the in-process McpServer) times out, so the bridge answers `workspace_unavailable`. Raising the test's probe timeout 200 ms -> 2000 ms does not help: the request never completes. Plain loopback HTTP between processes works (3 ms), and the runtime-only MCP tests pass. Cause not found yet; proposed as its own session.

rm build.pid && git add src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/Bridge/CMakeLists.txt && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Build the MCP bridge with the project's Asio setting, so its tests stop hanging

The 7 "MCP bridge ..." cases in agent_bridge_tests failed on macOS and then
hung forever in the test Harness destructor, so a full run never finished.

Cause: c177a160b3 linked boost_libs into agent_bridge_tests for Boost.Log.
That brought BOOST_ASIO_DISABLE_KQUEUE (set project-wide on macOS through
boost_headeronly) to the test files and McpServer.cpp, but not to
jusprin_mcp_bridge_core (Bridge.cpp, HttpExchange.cpp), which was still
built for Asio's kqueue reactor. One binary held both reactors' inline code
(20 kqueue_reactor and 13 select_reactor symbols), and the linker mixed
them. The bridge's io thread ran a select reactor while its connect was
registered with a kqueue reactor nobody polled: the liveness probe timed
out, the bridge answered workspace_unavailable, and the never-finished
operation kept io_context::run() alive, so Server::stop() waited in
join() forever.

Fix: jusprin_mcp_bridge_core links boost_headeronly PUBLIC, so it and
everything that links it compile Asio the same way. The shipped
jusprin-mcp executable on macOS now uses the select reactor like the
rest of the app (it holds at most 16 connections).

Tests (Release, this Mac):
- Before: "MCP bridge serves modern discovery..." failed (isError true)
  and the process hung in ~Harness at ~0 CPU.
- After: the 7 "MCP bridge*" cases pass in 5 random orders (84 assertions
  each). The whole agent_bridge_tests binary, no filter, random order,
  passes twice: 468 test cases, 16397 assertions, 2-3 s.
- jusprin-mcp rebuilt: no kqueue_reactor code; an offline stdin session
  (initialize, workspace_inspect) answers and exits cleanly.
EOF
